chainlinkOracle.purpose: Testnet mirror of the C-6 launch oracle (see base-mainnet.json.chainlinkOracle). Lets the Chainlink-direct pivot run a full lifecycle/soak/canary on Base Sepolia BEFORE mainnet - the first time the pivot touches a chain. Deploy with DeployChainlinkOracle.s.sol, verify with scripts/verify-chainlink-oracle.mjs (CONFIG=contracts/config/base-sepolia.json), then set BLESSED_ORACLES for Deploy.s.sol.
chainlinkOracle.verifiedOnChain: Read from Base Sepolia 2026-08-29 and matched: ETH/USD proxy 0x4aDC..7cb1 decimals()==8, description()=='ETH / USD', latestRoundData answer ~$2,433 fresh (307s); LINK/USD proxy 0xb113..5A61 decimals()==8, description()=='LINK / USD', answer ~$11.30 fresh (1055s). Both proxies carry code (19144 B). Re-run the verifier before deploying (read-only, no key).
chainlinkOracle.sequencerUptimeFeedNote: Intentionally EMPTY (address(0)) on this testnet: ChainlinkOracle skips the sequencer guard off a configured sequencer chain, and the guard itself is exercised by ChainlinkOracle.t.sol with a mock (down / within-grace / up) - a stronger test than a live testnet feed. The testnet exercise targets the vault lifecycle + real-feed pricing, not the L2 uptime gate. The mainnet block (base-mainnet.json) carries the REAL verified Base sequencer feed, which is MANDATORY there. This is a deliberate testnet/mainnet asymmetry, not a missing address.
chainlinkOracle.usdcPinNote: USDC (0x036C..CF7e = config `usdc`) pinned to 1e18 in ChainlinkOracle. Do NOT also list USDC in assets (the constructor rejects that).

assets.aggregatorPinNote: The aggregator implementation this EACAggregatorProxy pointed at when the config was last verified on-chain, plus the proxy's phaseId (which Chainlink increments on every swap). Chainlink swaps the aggregator behind a proxy as routine operation and ChainlinkOracle caches `scale` from decimals() ONCE at construction, so this pin is how a swap becomes VISIBLE. scripts/verify-chainlink-oracle.mjs reports a change as DRIFT, never as a failure -- a swap is legitimate. The safety verdict stays with the `decimals() == 8` check next to it, which is a complete test of the residual: if decimals is still 8, a deployed oracle's cached scale is still correct however many swaps happened. Re-run the verifier on a cadence post-deploy, not only before deploying. See docs/LAUNCH-READINESS.md section 4 row 14.
assets.feedDescriptionOnChainNote: The EXACT string the proxy returns from description(). Machine-compared by scripts/verify-chainlink-oracle.mjs (equality, not a substring) so a plausible-but-wrong feed - right pair, wrong deployment - fails before deploy. ChainlinkOracle enforces the weaker on-chain invariant that it ends in a USD quote leg.
assets.heartbeatNote: 24h staleness bound (== maxStalenessSeconds). DELIBERATELY generous vs mainnet's 3600: Base Sepolia feeds update irregularly with no economic SLA, so a tight bound would false-freeze a multi-hour soak on testnet-feed flakiness rather than a protocol bug. Mainnet WETH uses 3600.
assets.bandNote: sane-price band $100 .. $100,000 (WAD), same as mainnet WETH. Testnet ETH/USD ~ $2,433 at verification - comfortably inside.

assets.heartbeatNote: 24h staleness bound (testnet-generous, see WETH). LINK stands in for the second mainnet asset (cbBTC) - Base Sepolia has no cbBTC feed, but LINK/USD is a live 8-decimal Chainlink feed, which is all the pivot exercise needs.

chainlinkOracle.legacyAssetsNote: The top-level `assets` block below is the DEPRECATED custom-OracleAggregator shape (quorum + 3 adapters over one feed - the `testnetCompromise`). C-6 replaced that whole path with this chainlinkOracle block. `assets` is retained only for the legacy deploy path / historical reference; the launch path is chainlinkOracle.
verification: For each asset feed: code.length > 0; decimals() == 8 (Chainlink USD-feed convention); latestRoundData answer > 0 and updatedAt fresh within heartbeatSeconds.

DENOMINATION: description() must be USD-quoted (ends in ' USD' or '/USD') AND equal feedDescriptionOnChain exactly. ChainlinkOracle's constructor enforces the USD quote leg + 8 decimals on-chain; this verifier adds the exact-string match.
sequencerUptimeFeed empty on this testnet (guard skipped) - acceptable for the testnet exercise ONLY; mainnet requires it.
USDC not also present in assets[].

Heartbeat and band are BOUNDED ON-CHAIN by the ChainlinkOracle constructor: heartbeatSeconds in [600, 86400]; an enabled band needs minPriceWad > 0, maxPriceWad > minPriceWad, maxPriceWad <= 1000 * minPriceWad, and it must contain the feed's current answer. Off-chain verification is no longer the only thing standing between a typo and a permanently mis-parameterised immutable oracle.

testnetCompromise: Base Sepolia has exactly ONE Chainlink feed per pair, so the >=3-source constructor floor is met by deploying three ChainlinkSourceAdapter instances over the same canonical feed (distinct source addresses). This satisfies the OracleAggregator constructor mechanically but NOT the SF-1 mechanism-diversity listing criterion, and M-1's distinctness check cannot catch it either: the ADDRESSES differ, the upstream feed does not. Quorum is 3-of-3 since the H-1 remediation (quorum must reach MIN_MEDIAN=3, because a 2-element lower median is a minimum); on this testnet that costs nothing, as all three adapters read one feed and fail together anyway. A mainnet config MUST list >=5 sources per asset with quorum 3 - see base-mainnet.json oracleRemediationRequired.

smoke.minDepositNote: 1 USDC is a TESTNET SMOKE value, kept small so the smoke lifecycle stays cheap; the deployed Base Sepolia smoke vault already uses it. A PRODUCTION vault must set minDepositUsdc to an economically meaningful value (see base-mainnet.json minDepositNote and AI-AUDIT-REPORT.md H-8): the <5-member signer quorum regime is stake-blind, so a 1-USDC seat lets an attacker buy the regime flip or grief a small vault into ungovernability. Documented listing constraint, not a contract floor (M-6 shape).
smoke.govDefencesNote: M-6: these three were 0 / 10000 / 0 — i.e. the reference configuration shipped with every named CM-6/VO-5 defence DISABLED. proposalThresholdBps 0 let anyone holding one unit open proposals (the precondition M-7 and C-1 both rely on); concentrationCapBps 10000 let a single delegate carry 100% of snapshot stake, so one live participant plus a permissionless cranker manufactured full quorum from offline delegators, defeating VO-2 outright; proposalCooldown was not validated by the contract AT ALL. Governance._validateConfig now enforces a 100 bps threshold floor, a 5000 bps concentration ceiling, and a proposalCooldown in [1 hour, 30 days] — the upper bound because an unvalidated uint32 cooldown is C-2's shape on a field C-2 did not cover.
smoke.govTestnetNote: Set AT the contract floors here, unlike base-mainnet.json which sits deliberately above them. A testnet smoke run wants the least friction that is still legal; mainnet capital wants margin.
